cases.summary: Single-lesion paucibacillary leprosy in a child. The case is about proportionality: correct classification prevents both overtreatment with a 12-month multibacillary regimen and undertreatment that risks relapse, and it addresses paediatric dosing and minocycline avoidance.

summary_i18n.en: Single-lesion paucibacillary leprosy in a child - correct classification, paediatric dosing, and avoiding both over- and undertreatment.
summary_i18n.de: Paucibazilläre Einzelläsion bei einem Kind - korrekte Klassifikation, pädiatrische Dosierung und Vermeidung von Über- wie Untertherapie.
summary_i18n.es: Lepra paucibacilar de lesión única en un niño: clasificación correcta, dosificación pediátrica y evitar tanto el sobretratamiento como el infratratamiento.
summary_i18n.nl: Paucibacillaire lepra met één laesie bij een kind - juiste classificatie, pediatrische dosering en zowel over- als onderbehandeling vermijden.
summary_i18n.ru: Паучибациллярная лепра с одиночным очагом у ребёнка: правильная классификация, педиатрические дозы, недопущение избыточного и недостаточного лечения.

cases.author: MedSimQA Editorial

patient.region: Endemic district; father treated for multibacillary leprosy two years ago

presentation.chief_complaint: A pale patch on the left cheek noticed by a teacher during a school screening programme; the child had not noticed it.

chief_complaint_i18n.en: A pale patch on the left cheek found at school screening; the child had not noticed it.
chief_complaint_i18n.de: Blasser Herd an der linken Wange bei einer Schulreihenuntersuchung entdeckt; dem Kind nicht aufgefallen.
chief_complaint_i18n.es: Mancha pálida en la mejilla izquierda detectada en un cribado escolar; el niño no la había notado.
chief_complaint_i18n.nl: Bleke plek op de linkerwang gevonden bij schoolscreening; het kind had het niet opgemerkt.
chief_complaint_i18n.ru: Бледное пятно на левой щеке выявлено при школьном скрининге; ребёнок его не замечал.

presentation.history_of_present_illness: The patch has been present for at least eight months according to his mother. It does not itch, does not scale and has not changed in size. He is systemically well, growing normally and performing well at school. His father completed multibacillary MDT two years ago, making this child a household contact - the reason the school programme flagged him for examination.
past_medical_history: Fully immunised including BCG at birth (BCG scar present)
family_history: Father: multibacillary leprosy, completed MDT 2 years ago
presentation.social_history: Lives with both parents and three siblings in a two-room dwelling. Attends primary school.

review_of_systems.dermatological: One hypopigmented patch; no other lesions on full-body examination in good light
review_of_systems.neurological: No weakness, no other sensory loss; no complaints

examination_findings: ONE well-defined hypopigmented macule, 4 cm diameter, on the left cheek, with a dry non-sweating surface and a slightly raised margin
Complete loss of light touch and pinprick sensation within the patch, with normal sensation immediately outside it
Full-body examination in good natural light found no other lesions - essential, since classification depends on lesion count
All peripheral nerves palpated: NO thickening and NO tenderness of ulnar, median, radial cutaneous, common peroneal, posterior tibial or great auricular nerves
Voluntary muscle testing normal in all groups; monofilament testing normal on hands and feet

microbiology.microscopy: Slit-skin smears NEGATIVE for acid-fast bacilli at all sites. Biopsy of the lesion edge shows well-formed epithelioid granulomas with Langhans giant cells tracking along dermal nerves, dense peripheral lymphocytic cuffing, and destruction of a dermal nerve twig. No bacilli seen on Fite staining.

molecular_findings.interpretation: Confirms M. leprae despite negative microscopy. Granulomas tracking along dermal nerves with nerve destruction is essentially pathognomonic of leprosy and would suffice for diagnosis even without PCR.

microbiology.interpretation: Smear-negative paucibacillary leprosy, tuberculoid pole, in a child. Single lesion, no nerve involvement, negative smears: this classifies as single-lesion paucibacillary disease. Correct classification is the whole clinical decision here, because it determines whether the child receives 6 or 12 months of therapy.

microbiology.microscopy: Not repeated - smears were negative and are not indicated for monitoring paucibacillary disease.
microbiology.interpretation: Lesion flattened and repigmenting; sensation partially recovered within the patch. No new lesions, no nerve involvement. Treatment complete and successful. Note that sensory recovery in a small patch is common in children and is not expected in adults with established nerve damage.

results.interference_note: Checked before dapsone. Particularly important in a child, in whom haemolysis is less well tolerated and less likely to be reported.
Minimal fall on dapsone in a G6PD-normal child, as expected.

protocols.name: Paediatric paucibacillary multidrug therapy with contact management
protocols.guideline_source: WHO 2018 leprosy guidelines - paediatric dosing and post-exposure prophylaxis
protocols.indication: Single-lesion paucibacillary leprosy in a child of 24 kg with no nerve involvement.

regimen.dose: 450 mg (10-20 mg/kg, child 10-14 years dosing band adjusted for weight)
regimen.notes: WHO now recommends the standard three-drug regimen for paucibacillary disease as well, harmonising PB and MB treatment. Paediatric blister packs exist for the 10-14 year band; below that, dose by weight.

regimen.dose: 150 mg monthly and 50 mg on alternate days
regimen.notes: Now included in paucibacillary regimens under the 2018 guidelines. Discuss pigmentation with the family before starting - in a school-age child this is a genuine and predictable cause of stigma and non-adherence.
Contraindicated under 12 years because of permanent dental staining and effects on developing bone. This forecloses the usual ROM (rifampicin-ofloxacin-minocycline) alternative in young children.

regimen.agent: Single-dose rifampicin post-exposure prophylaxis for contacts
regimen.dose: 10-20 mg/kg by age band, single dose
regimen.notes: Offered to household and neighbourhood contacts aged 2 years and over after leprosy has been excluded in each. Reduces contact incidence by roughly 50-60% over two years. The index case himself is a contact of his father, which is how he was found.

monitoring: Monthly clinical review with full skin and nerve examination - nerve function is the outcome that matters
Slit-skin smears are NOT needed for monitoring paucibacillary disease
Growth and school attendance: treatment must not become a reason for exclusion or stigma
Counsel the family that a patch may take months to repigment and that this is not treatment failure
Annual review for 2 years after completion to detect late reaction or relapse
contraindications: Minocycline and other tetracyclines under 12 years
adverse_effects: Clofazimine pigmentation - the dominant adherence issue in children
Rifampicin orange discolouration of urine and tears, which must be explained in advance to avoid alarm
protocols.notes: Paediatric leprosy is a sentinel indicator of ongoing community transmission. A child with leprosy means recent transmission, and the public health response - contact tracing and prophylaxis - matters as much as this child's own treatment.

diagnoses.label: Single-lesion paucibacillary (tuberculoid) leprosy in a child

label_i18n.en: Single-lesion paucibacillary leprosy in a child
label_i18n.de: Paucibazilläre Lepra mit Einzelläsion bei einem Kind
label_i18n.es: Lepra paucibacilar de lesión única en un niño
label_i18n.nl: Paucibacillaire lepra met één laesie bij een kind
label_i18n.ru: Паучибациллярная лепра с одиночным очагом у ребёнка

diagnoses.discriminator: A single anaesthetic hypopigmented patch with negative smears, no nerve thickening, and a biopsy showing granulomas tracking along dermal nerves with nerve destruction.
supporting_evidence: One well-defined hypopigmented macule with complete sensory loss and absent sweating
Slit-skin smears negative at all sites, bacterial index 0
No nerve thickening or tenderness anywhere
Epithelioid granulomas along dermal nerves with nerve destruction on biopsy
RLEP PCR positive
Household contact of a treated multibacillary case
Complete response to 6 months of paucibacillary MDT

diagnoses.label: Pityriasis alba
diagnoses.discriminator: The commonest mimic in children and the reason many cases are missed. Pityriasis alba is scaly, has indistinct margins, and crucially has NORMAL sensation and sweating.
supporting_evidence: Hypopigmented facial patch in a child
refuting_evidence: Complete sensory loss within the patch

diagnoses.label: Vitiligo
diagnoses.discriminator: Vitiligo is completely depigmented (chalk-white) rather than hypopigmented, and sensation is entirely normal.
supporting_evidence: Pale facial patch

diagnoses.label: Multibacillary leprosy requiring 12 months of therapy
diagnoses.discriminator: The overtreatment error. Classification rests on lesion count, nerve involvement and smear status - one lesion, no nerve involvement and negative smears is paucibacillary. Treating this child for 12 months would double clofazimine exposure and pigmentation for no benefit.

teaching_points: Sensory testing of the lesion is the diagnostic manoeuvre. An anaesthetic hypopigmented patch is leprosy until proven otherwise, and a patch with normal sensation almost never is.
Examine the whole body in good light and palpate every accessible peripheral nerve. Classification depends on lesion count and nerve involvement, and classification determines treatment duration.
Leprosy in a child is a sentinel event indicating recent community transmission. The public health response matters as much as the individual treatment.
Minocycline and other tetracyclines are contraindicated under 12 years, which removes the usual ROM alternative regimen from the paediatric toolkit.
Check G6PD before dapsone, particularly in a child who may not report symptoms of haemolysis reliably.
Warn the family in advance about clofazimine pigmentation and rifampicin-orange urine and tears. Unexplained, both cause alarm and non-adherence; explained, neither does.
Single-dose rifampicin post-exposure prophylaxis for contacts aged 2 and over reduces incidence by roughly half over two years, and leprosy must be excluded in each contact before it is given.
Repigmentation takes months after cure. Warn the family, or a resolving patch will be read as treatment failure.

references.citation: WHO Guidelines for the Diagnosis, Treatment and Prevention of Leprosy. 2018.
Moet FJ et al. Effectiveness of single dose rifampicin in preventing leprosy in close contacts (COLEP). BMJ 2008.

must_include_findings.label: Household contact of a treated case

safety_rules.description: Must not recommend minocycline or another tetracycline in a child under 12.
Should recommend contact tracing and post-exposure prophylaxis.
Must not recommend a 12-month multibacillary course for single-lesion paucibacillary disease.

cases.title: Leprosy, HIV and pregnancy: three regimens colliding

title_i18n.en: Leprosy, HIV and pregnancy: three regimens colliding
title_i18n.de: Lepra, HIV und Schwangerschaft: drei kollidierende Therapieschemata
title_i18n.es: Lepra, VIH y embarazo: tres regímenes en conflicto

title_i18n.ru: Лепра, ВИЧ и беременность: столкновение трёх схем лечения

cases.summary: Multibacillary leprosy in a pregnant woman starting antiretroviral therapy. The case is built around the rifampicin-antiretroviral interaction, teratogenicity constraints, and immune reconstitution precipitating a type 1 reaction.

summary_i18n.en: Multibacillary leprosy in pregnancy with new HIV diagnosis - rifampicin-ART interaction, teratogenicity limits and immune reconstitution reaction.
summary_i18n.de: Multibazilläre Lepra in der Schwangerschaft bei Erstdiagnose HIV - Rifampicin-ART-Interaktion, Teratogenitätsgrenzen und Immunrekonstitutionsreaktion.
summary_i18n.es: Lepra multibacilar en el embarazo con VIH de nuevo diagnóstico: interacción rifampicina-TAR, límites por teratogenicidad y reacción por reconstitución inmune.
summary_i18n.nl: Multibacillaire lepra in de zwangerschap bij nieuwe hiv-diagnose - rifampicine-ART-interactie, teratogeniteitsgrenzen en immuunreconstitutiereactie.
summary_i18n.ru: Мультибациллярная лепра при беременности и впервые выявленной ВИЧ-инфекции: взаимодействие рифампицина с АРТ, ограничения по тератогенности и реакция иммунного восстановления.

cases.author: MedSimQA Editorial

patient.region: Endemic region with high HIV prevalence

presentation.chief_complaint: Newly diagnosed multibacillary leprosy at 18 weeks of pregnancy, with HIV diagnosed on the same day at antenatal booking.

chief_complaint_i18n.en: Newly diagnosed multibacillary leprosy at 18 weeks pregnant, with HIV diagnosed the same day.
chief_complaint_i18n.de: Neu diagnostizierte multibazilläre Lepra in der 18. Schwangerschaftswoche, HIV am selben Tag festgestellt.
chief_complaint_i18n.es: Lepra multibacilar de nuevo diagnóstico a las 18 semanas de embarazo, con VIH diagnosticado el mismo día.
chief_complaint_i18n.nl: Nieuw gediagnosticeerde multibacillaire lepra bij 18 weken zwangerschap, met dezelfde dag een hiv-diagnose.
chief_complaint_i18n.ru: Впервые выявленная мультибациллярная лепра на 18-й неделе беременности; в тот же день диагностирована ВИЧ-инфекция.

presentation.history_of_present_illness: She presented to antenatal booking with a two-year history of enlarging skin patches, now numerous and infiltrated, with numbness of both feet. Routine antenatal HIV testing was positive, with a CD4 count of 180 cells/µL and a viral load of 340,000 copies/mL. She therefore requires antiretroviral therapy, multibacillary leprosy treatment and safe obstetric care simultaneously, and each constrains the others.
presentation.social_history: Farm worker. Partner's HIV status unknown; partner notification and testing arranged.

review_of_systems.dermatological: Numerous infiltrated hypopigmented and erythematous plaques on trunk and limbs
review_of_systems.neurological: Bilateral glove-and-stocking sensory loss; no motor deficit at presentation
review_of_systems.obstetric: Fetal movements felt; no bleeding, no contractions
review_of_systems.general: Weight appropriate for gestation; no fever, no night sweats, no cough

examination_findings: Multiple (more than 20) infiltrated, hypopigmented and erythematous plaques on trunk and limbs
Bilateral ulnar and posterior tibial nerve thickening, non-tender at presentation
Glove-and-stocking sensory loss with intact motor function (MRC 5/5 throughout)
Uterus consistent with 18 weeks; fetal heart rate 148 bpm
No oral candidiasis, no lymphadenopathy, no hepatosplenomegaly

molecular_findings.interpretation: Fully susceptible. Standard MB-MDT is appropriate, which simplifies one of the three competing problems.

microbiology.interpretation: Fully susceptible multibacillary leprosy with a high bacillary load. Standard MB-MDT is indicated; the complexity lies entirely in the interactions and the pregnancy, not in the organism.
Morphological index falling rapidly. Bacillary killing is proceeding normally despite HIV co-infection, which is the expected pattern - HIV does not impair the response of leprosy to MDT.

results.interference_note: Anaemia of pregnancy plus chronic infection. Relevant because dapsone will add a haemolytic burden.
Normal, so dapsone can be used. Note that female heterozygotes can give intermediate results because of lyonisation, so a borderline value would need genotyping.
Routine at a CD4 below 200 before starting antiretroviral therapy.
Tuberculosis must be excluded before starting rifampicin-containing therapy in an HIV-positive patient - undiagnosed TB treated with monthly rifampicin alone would generate rifampicin-resistant TB.

lab_panels.comment: Three months on dolutegravir-based ART with a doubled dolutegravir dose because of rifampicin.

results.interference_note: Falling appropriately. The dose adjustment is working; without it, rifampicin induction of UGT1A1 and CYP3A4 would have roughly halved dolutegravir exposure and risked virological failure with integrase resistance.
Rising CD4 count - which is also what precipitates the immune reconstitution reaction seen at week 8.

lab_panels.comment: Eight weeks after starting ART: existing plaques became inflamed and both ulnar nerves became tender.

results.analyte_name: Voluntary muscle test - right little finger abduction
results.interference_note: New motor deficit - the threshold for corticosteroid regardless of pregnancy.
Immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome presenting as a type 1 leprosy reaction - a recognised consequence of the rising CD4 count.

imaging.findings: Single viable intrauterine pregnancy at 18+2 weeks. Growth on the 45th centile. Normal anatomy survey. Normal liquor volume and umbilical artery Doppler.
imaging.impression: Normal fetus. Serial growth scans arranged, since corticosteroid, chronic infection and HIV all carry fetal growth implications.

protocols.name: Concurrent MB-MDT, antiretroviral therapy and reaction management in pregnancy
protocols.guideline_source: Composite of WHO 2018 leprosy guidelines, WHO HIV treatment guidelines and obstetric practice
protocols.indication: Multibacillary leprosy with newly diagnosed HIV (CD4 180) at 18 weeks of pregnancy, complicated by an immune reconstitution type 1 reaction at week 8.

regimen.notes: SAFE in pregnancy. Give vitamin K to the mother in the last weeks and to the neonate at birth, since rifampicin can cause neonatal haemorrhagic disease.
Considered safe in pregnancy. Crosses the placenta and causes reversible neonatal skin pigmentation - the parents must be told in advance or it causes real distress at delivery.

Safe in pregnancy. Adds to the anaemia; folate supplementation is continued. G6PD is normal. Neonatal haemolysis and kernicterus are a theoretical risk if given close to delivery in a G6PD-deficient infant.

regimen.duration: revert to once daily 2 weeks after rifampicin stops
regimen.notes: THE central interaction. Rifampicin induces UGT1A1 and CYP3A4 and roughly halves dolutegravir exposure; the dose must be doubled or virological failure and integrase resistance follow.
No clinically significant interaction with rifampicin.

Rifampicin reduces boosted protease inhibitor concentrations by up to 80%. If a protease inhibitor is unavoidable, rifabutin substitutes for rifampicin - but only if the strain is rifamycin-susceptible.

Started for the new motor deficit. Prednisolone is largely inactivated by placental 11-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase, so fetal exposure is limited and it is the corticosteroid of choice in pregnancy. Nerve preservation outweighs the fetal growth risk here.
Even if a type 2 reaction were to develop. In pregnancy the alternatives are corticosteroid, high-dose clofazimine and, if needed, pentoxifylline.
CD4 180. Note that co-trimoxazole plus dapsone compounds the haemolysis and methaemoglobinaemia risk, and the haemoglobin must be watched.

monitoring: HIV viral load at 3 and 6 months - the readout on whether the dolutegravir dose adjustment is adequate
Full blood count monthly: pregnancy, HIV, dapsone and co-trimoxazole all contribute to anaemia
Methaemoglobin if cyanosis or unexplained breathlessness develops
Nerve function assessment at every visit - the reaction is the main threat to long-term function
Serial fetal growth scans, given corticosteroid exposure and chronic infection
Vitamin K to the mother in late pregnancy and to the neonate at birth
Revert dolutegravir to once daily 2 weeks after rifampicin is stopped - a step that is very easy to forget
Infant follow-up: HIV PCR per protocol, and reassurance about reversible clofazimine pigmentation
contraindications: Minocycline and other tetracyclines in pregnancy
adverse_effects: Anaemia from combined dapsone, co-trimoxazole and pregnancy; neonatal pigmentation from clofazimine; neonatal haemorrhagic disease from rifampicin; corticosteroid effects on fetal growth and maternal glucose
protocols.notes: HIV co-infection does not alter the leprosy regimen or its duration, and leprosy is not an AIDS-defining illness. What HIV changes is the interaction landscape and the likelihood of an immune reconstitution reaction, which occurred here at week 8.

diagnoses.label: Multibacillary leprosy with HIV co-infection in pregnancy, complicated by an immune reconstitution type 1 reaction

label_i18n.en: Multibacillary leprosy with HIV co-infection in pregnancy and immune reconstitution type 1 reaction
label_i18n.de: Multibazilläre Lepra mit HIV-Koinfektion in der Schwangerschaft und Typ-1-Immunrekonstitutionsreaktion
label_i18n.es: Lepra multibacilar con coinfección por VIH en el embarazo y reacción de tipo 1 por reconstitución inmune
label_i18n.nl: Multibacillaire lepra met hiv-co-infectie in de zwangerschap en type 1 immuunreconstitutiereactie
label_i18n.ru: Мультибациллярная лепра с ВИЧ-коинфекцией при беременности, осложнённая реакцией 1-го типа на фоне иммунного восстановления

diagnoses.discriminator: Smear-positive multibacillary disease with a bacterial index of 4.8, concurrent untreated HIV with a CD4 of 180, and a type 1 reaction emerging eight weeks after antiretroviral therapy as the CD4 count rose.
supporting_evidence: More than 20 lesions with bacterial index 4.8 and morphological index 22%
CD4 180 cells/µL with viral load 340,000 copies/mL
Type 1 reaction at week 8 of ART with a rising CD4 count
Existing lesions inflamed with new nerve tenderness and motor deficit
Wild-type resistance targets throughout
Appropriate virological and bacteriological response on adjusted therapy

diagnoses.label: Tuberculosis co-infection
diagnoses.discriminator: Must be actively excluded before any rifampicin-containing regimen in an HIV-positive patient. Undiagnosed tuberculosis exposed to monthly rifampicin alone would generate rifampicin-resistant TB.
supporting_evidence: HIV with CD4 180 in a high-burden setting
refuting_evidence: No cough, fever or night sweats

diagnoses.label: Type 2 reaction (erythema nodosum leprosum)
diagnoses.discriminator: Her bacillary load puts her at real risk of ENL later in treatment. It would matter enormously, because thalidomide - the most effective treatment - is absolutely contraindicated in pregnancy and the alternatives are weaker.
supporting_evidence: High bacterial index is the main risk factor for ENL
refuting_evidence: Current reaction involves existing lesions without fever, nodules or systemic features

diagnoses.label: Antiretroviral drug failure from non-adherence
diagnoses.discriminator: The default explanation for a slow viral load decline, and wrong here. The relevant question was whether the dolutegravir dose had been adjusted for rifampicin - a pharmacological problem, not a behavioural one.
supporting_evidence: Viral load not fully suppressed at 3 months
refuting_evidence: Viral load fell from 340,000 to 120 copies/mL

teaching_points: Rifampicin is a potent inducer of CYP3A4 and UGT1A1. Dolutegravir must be doubled to twice-daily dosing while rifampicin is given, and reverted two weeks after it stops - a step that is very easy to forget and that causes unnecessary toxicity if missed.
Boosted protease inhibitors cannot be combined with rifampicin; concentrations fall by up to 80%. Rifabutin is the substitute, but only where the strain is rifamycin-susceptible.

Exclude tuberculosis before starting a rifampicin-containing regimen in any HIV-positive patient. Monthly rifampicin against undiagnosed TB is effectively intermittent monotherapy and generates rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis.
MB-MDT is safe in pregnancy: rifampicin, clofazimine and dapsone are all used. Thalidomide and the tetracyclines are not.

Immune reconstitution after starting antiretroviral therapy commonly presents as a type 1 leprosy reaction, typically within the first three months as the CD4 count rises. It is treated as any type 1 reaction, with corticosteroid, and antiretroviral therapy is continued.

Prednisolone is the corticosteroid of choice in pregnancy because placental 11-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase largely inactivates it, limiting fetal exposure. Preserving nerve function outweighs the growth risk when there is a new motor deficit.
Warn the parents in advance that clofazimine crosses the placenta and causes reversible neonatal skin pigmentation, and give vitamin K to mother and neonate because of rifampicin.
HIV does not change the leprosy regimen or its duration, and it does not impair the bacteriological response. What it changes is the interaction landscape and the risk of reactions.

references.citation: WHO Guidelines for the Diagnosis, Treatment and Prevention of Leprosy. 2018.
WHO Consolidated Guidelines on HIV Prevention, Testing, Treatment, Service Delivery and Monitoring. 2021.
Deps P, Lockwood DNJ. Leprosy occurring as immune reconstitution syndrome. Trans R Soc Trop Med Hyg.

must_include_findings.label: Immune reconstitution presenting as a type 1 reaction
Corticosteroid for the new motor deficit

expected_management: vitamin k for mother and neonate
revert dolutegravir dose after rifampicin stops

critical_values.reason: Advanced HIV requiring opportunistic infection prophylaxis
New motor deficit requiring urgent corticosteroid

cases.summary: Molecular epidemiology as a clinical tool. VNTR typing shows a DIFFERENT strain from the original episode, establishing reinfection - which reframes the problem from a treatment failure into an ongoing transmission failure and changes the public health response.

summary_i18n.en: VNTR typing shows a different strain, establishing reinfection rather than relapse - reframing a treatment failure as a transmission failure.
summary_i18n.de: VNTR-Typisierung zeigt einen anderen Stamm und belegt eine Reinfektion statt eines Rezidivs - aus einem Therapieversagen wird ein Übertragungsproblem.
summary_i18n.es: La tipificación VNTR muestra una cepa distinta y establece reinfección en lugar de recaída, reencuadrando un fallo terapéutico como un fallo de transmisión.
summary_i18n.nl: VNTR-typering toont een andere stam en bewijst herinfectie in plaats van recidief - een behandelfalen wordt zo een transmissieprobleem.
summary_i18n.ru: VNTR-типирование выявляет другой штамм, подтверждая реинфекцию, а не рецидив: неудача лечения оказывается неудачей контроля передачи.

cases.author: MedSimQA Editorial

patient.region: Endemic coastal community with incomplete contact tracing

presentation.chief_complaint: New skin lesions and numb fingers seven years after being declared cured of multibacillary leprosy.

chief_complaint_i18n.en: New skin lesions and numb fingers seven years after being declared cured.
chief_complaint_i18n.de: Neue Hautläsionen und taube Finger sieben Jahre nach Heilungserklärung.
chief_complaint_i18n.es: Lesiones cutáneas nuevas y dedos adormecidos siete años después de ser declarado curado.
chief_complaint_i18n.nl: Nieuwe huidlaesies en gevoelloze vingers zeven jaar na genezenverklaring.
chief_complaint_i18n.ru: Новые кожные высыпания и онемение пальцев через семь лет после объявления об излечении.

presentation.history_of_present_illness: He completed 12 months of MB-MDT eight years ago with a documented fall in bacterial index from 3.6 to 1.2 and was declared cured. He remained well for seven years with annual reviews showing no new lesions. Over the last six months new hypopigmented and infiltrated lesions have appeared in previously unaffected sites, with progressive numbness of both hands. He has no fever, no tender nodules and no lesion tenderness. Two of his neighbours - not household members, and never traced or examined - were diagnosed with leprosy in the intervening years.
past_medical_history: Borderline lepromatous leprosy treated 8 years ago, BI 3.6 at diagnosis, declared cured after 12 months of MB-MDT
presentation.social_history: Fisherman working in close quarters on small boats. Lives in a dense coastal settlement where two neighbours were diagnosed with leprosy in the last seven years and were never formally traced as contacts of anyone.

review_of_systems.dermatological: New lesions in previously uninvolved sites; no tenderness
review_of_systems.neurological: Progressive numbness of both hands over 6 months; no acute pain, no motor loss yet
review_of_systems.general: Well, no fever, no weight loss

examination_findings: Eleven new hypopigmented and infiltrated plaques on the back, shoulders and thighs - anatomical sites uninvolved during the original episode, as documented in the archived body chart
Original lesion sites remain flat, repigmented and inactive
Bilateral ulnar nerve thickening, NON-tender, with grade 1 sensory impairment
No tender nodules, no fever, no uveitis

microbiology.microscopy: Acid-fast bacilli present in moderate numbers with a substantial proportion of solidly staining forms.

molecular_findings.interpretation: FULLY SUSCEPTIBLE. This is an important negative: a relapse after adequate treatment would more often carry a resistance mutation, and full susceptibility here points towards a newly acquired strain.

molecular_findings.result: Profile differs from the archived original isolate at 6 of 16 loci
molecular_findings.interpretation: A DIFFERENT STRAIN. This is reinfection, not relapse. The distinction is not academic: relapse implicates the treatment, whereas reinfection implicates ongoing community transmission and an incomplete contact-tracing programme.

molecular_findings.result: SNP subtype 4N; the original isolate was subtype 4P
molecular_findings.interpretation: Different subtype, independently confirming a distinct infecting strain.

microbiology.interpretation: Multibacillary leprosy caused by a strain genotypically distinct from the original infecting organism at 6 of 16 VNTR loci and of a different SNP subtype. This is REINFECTION with a fully susceptible strain. Standard MB-MDT is indicated, and the significant finding for the health system is that transmission is continuing in this community.

results.interference_note: G6PD DEFICIENT - and he received dapsone for 12 months during his original treatment without ever being tested. He tolerated it, which happens with the milder African A- variant, but it must not be repeated now that it is known.

results.value_text: Hemizygous G6PD A- (V68M/N126D), WHO class III
results.interference_note: The African A- variant causes self-limiting haemolysis of older cells only, unlike the Mediterranean variant in HEM-003. It is still a contraindication to a 12-month dapsone course.

imaging.findings: Bilateral ulnar nerve enlargement (16 mm2 right, 15 mm2 left) with no intraneural hypervascularity on power Doppler.
imaging.impression: Chronic thickening without acute neuritis - consistent with bacillary infiltration rather than a reaction, and therefore not an indication for corticosteroid.

protocols.name: Standard MB-MDT for reinfection, with a dapsone-free substitution and a community transmission response
protocols.guideline_source: WHO 2018 leprosy guidelines including alternative regimens and post-exposure prophylaxis
protocols.indication: Reinfection with fully susceptible M. leprae in a G6PD-deficient patient, with evidence of ongoing community transmission.

regimen.notes: Fully susceptible strain, so first-line therapy is appropriate. Reinfection is NOT a reason to reach for a second-line regimen.
SUBSTITUTED FOR DAPSONE because of G6PD deficiency. gyrA is wild type so the substitution is sound. Baseline ECG performed given the clofazimine-ofloxacin QT combination.
G6PD deficient. He tolerated dapsone eight years ago with the milder A- variant, but a 12-month re-exposure with the deficiency now documented would be indefensible.
Extended beyond the household to neighbours and boat crew. Two previously untraced neighbourhood cases are the likely source and mark a programme failure.

regimen.dose: 600 mg adults, weight-banded in children aged 2 and over
regimen.notes: Offered to traced contacts after leprosy has been excluded in each. Reduces incidence by roughly 50-60% over two years.

monitoring: Slit-skin smears at 6 and 12 months for bacterial and morphological index
ECG at baseline and 1 month for the clofazimine-ofloxacin QT combination
Document G6PD deficiency prominently and permanently in the record - it was missed once already
Programme-level review: two untraced neighbourhood cases represent a systems failure, not a patient failure
adverse_effects: Clofazimine pigmentation; ofloxacin tendinopathy, QT prolongation and peripheral neuropathy which is hard to distinguish from leprosy neuropathy
protocols.notes: The molecular typing changed the response at every level. Relapse would have prompted a review of his original treatment and resistance testing as the priority; reinfection prompts a community transmission investigation and a prophylaxis campaign.

diagnoses.discriminator: VNTR profile differing at 6 of 16 loci and a different SNP subtype from the archived original isolate, with a fully susceptible strain, new lesions at previously uninvolved sites, and a seven-year disease-free interval.
supporting_evidence: VNTR differs at 6 of 16 loci from the archived original isolate
SNP subtype 4N versus the original 4P
All resistance targets wild type - unusual for a true relapse after adequate treatment
Seven-year disease-free interval with documented annual reviews
New lesions at anatomical sites uninvolved originally, with the original sites inactive
Two untraced neighbourhood cases providing a plausible transmission source

diagnoses.label: Relapse of the original infection
diagnoses.discriminator: Clinically indistinguishable at the bedside, which is exactly why molecular typing is needed. Excluded by the different VNTR profile and SNP subtype. The distinction determines whether the health system reviews its treatment or its transmission control.
supporting_evidence: Previously treated patient with new active disease and a positive smear

diagnoses.label: Late type 1 reaction
diagnoses.discriminator: Type 1 reactions can occur years after cure and are the standard alternative to relapse. Excluded here by NEW lesions rather than inflammation of old ones, the absence of tenderness, the absence of intraneural hypervascularity, and above all by a bacterial index of 3.4 with a morphological index of 16%.
supporting_evidence: Reactions can occur years after treatment completion
refuting_evidence: New lesions in new sites rather than inflamed old lesions
No tenderness of lesions or nerves
Morphological index 16% indicating viable multiplying bacilli

teaching_points: Relapse and reinfection are clinically indistinguishable. Only molecular strain typing separates them, and the answer changes what the health system does: relapse implicates treatment, reinfection implicates transmission control.
A fully susceptible strain in a previously treated patient argues for reinfection. True relapse after adequate therapy more often carries a resistance mutation.
Archive the original isolate or its molecular profile. Without the stored baseline, no comparison is possible and this question becomes unanswerable years later.
New lesions at previously uninvolved sites, with the original sites inactive, favour reinfection. An archived body chart from the first episode is what makes that observation possible.
Reinfection with a susceptible strain is treated with standard first-line MDT. It is not a reason to escalate to a second-line regimen.
Check G6PD before dapsone, every time. This patient received a full 12-month course without testing and got away with it because he carries the milder A- variant.

Contact tracing must extend beyond the household in dense communities. Two untraced neighbourhood cases here were a programme failure that produced a second episode of disease in an already-treated patient.
Single-dose rifampicin post-exposure prophylaxis reduces contact incidence by roughly 50-60% over two years, and leprosy must be excluded in each contact before it is given.
